figure_caption: Evaluation protocol at a glance. Simplex-valued softmax outputs from evaluator-generated synthetic families are split into calibration and test parts. The studied procedure (Mondrian LAC with gated domain-classifier weighting) and four evaluator baselines (LAC, APS, RAPS, class-wise LAC) produce label sets, which are scored on three axes (marginal under-coverage with weight 0.5, worst-slice under-coverage 0.25, set-size ratio 0.25) and checked by three negative controls. Scope is limited to the declared synthetic families.

panels.title: Evaluation protocol at a glance
panels.short_caption: Synthetic simplex outputs are split, handled by the gated Mondrian procedure and four evaluator baselines, scored on three weighted axes and gated by three negative controls; scope is synthetic families only.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: one left-to-right pipeline showing what is evaluated: simplex outputs from synthetic families go through a conformal procedure and evaluator-owned baselines to label sets, which are scored by a three-part weighted loss and validity-gated by three negative controls, all inside a boundary limited to synthetic families.

NODES (stable IDs):
- SCOPE (region): large dashed outer boundary enclosing every node below, small corner tag 'Synthetic families only'. Outside the boundary, bottom-right, a small muted excluded box NOREAL 'Real data: untested' (no edges to it).
- EVAL (region): a labelled grouping 'Evaluator-owned' (a light container, not a node) that encloses DATA, SPLIT, BASE, LOSS and CTRL; the studied procedure PROC sits inside SCOPE but OUTSIDE the EVAL container to make clear the evaluator owns data, baselines, loss and controls.
- DATA (sharp box = data): 'Softmax outputs' with the symbol $$p(x)\in\Delta^{K-1}$$ and a small simplex-triangle glyph (drawio triangle shape with three dots inside). Sub-caption line 'Synthetic families'.
- CAL (sharp box = data): 'Calibration'.
- TEST (sharp box = data): 'Test'. Two small tags stacked under it: 'Exchangeable' and 'Shifted'.
- PROC (large rounded box, the studied object, MOST IMPORTANT element), titled 'Gated Mondrian LAC'. Inside it, left to right: MON (rounded box) 'Mondrian LAC thresholds' -> GATE (diamond) 'Shift gate'. From GATE two exits: 'open' -> WGT (rounded box) 'Weighted thresholds'; 'closed' -> UNW (rounded box) 'Unweighted fallback'. Small tag on GATE: 'cross-fitted domain classifier'.
- BASE (rounded container grouping four small rounded boxes, SECOND IMPORTANCE): 'Baselines' containing B1 'LAC', B2 'APS', B3 'RAPS', B4 'Class-wise LAC'.
- SETS (sharp box = data/result): 'Label sets' with symbol $$\mathcal{C}(x)$$. Two inbound edges, one from PROC, one from BASE.
- Scoring block (inside EVAL): three term boxes stacked vertically, TERM1 'Marginal under-coverage', TERM2 'Worst-slice under-coverage', TERM3 'Set-size ratio'. A weighted-sum node SUM (circle with ⊕) collects them; each incoming edge carries its weight as the edge label: 0.5, 0.25, 0.25 (these are the only numbers on the canvas besides symbols). SUM -> SCORE (sharp box = result) 'Score'.
- DELTA (small rounded box, near SCORE): 'Margin vs best baseline'.
- CTRL (rounded container with three small boxes, THIRD IMPORTANCE): 'Negative controls' containing C1 'Permuted cal. labels', C2 'Shuffled test labels', C3 'Uniform inputs'. Output node VALID (small rounded box with check glyph ✓) 'Run valid'.

EDGES (source -> target, style, label):
- DATA -> CAL: solid, no label.
- DATA -> TEST: solid, no label.
- CAL -> PROC: solid, no label.
- TEST -> PROC: solid, no label.
- CAL -> BASE: solid, no label.
- TEST -> BASE: solid, no label.
- MON -> GATE: solid, no label.
- GATE -> WGT: solid, label 'open'.
- GATE -> UNW: solid, label 'closed'.
- PROC -> SETS: solid, no label (leaves from WGT and UNW through the PROC border).
- BASE -> SETS: solid, no label.
- SETS -> TERM1, SETS -> TERM2, SETS -> TERM3: solid, no label (fan-out).
- TERM1 -> SUM: solid, label '0.5'. TERM2 -> SUM: solid, label '0.25'. TERM3 -> SUM: solid, label '0.25'.
- SUM -> SCORE: solid, label '1 − loss' written as $$1-\ell$$.
- SCORE -> DELTA: solid, no label.
- C1 -> VALID, C2 -> VALID, C3 -> VALID: dashed (auxiliary check, not data flow), no labels.
- VALID -> SCORE: dashed, label 'gates'.
- C1 -> CAL, C2 -> TEST, C3 -> DATA: dashed, no labels, ONLY if routing stays free of crossings; otherwise omit these three and keep the C -> VALID edges.

SPATIAL LAYOUT (21:9, wide): five columns left to right inside SCOPE. Column 1: DATA centred vertically. Column 2: CAL above TEST. Column 3 (widest): PROC on top, BASE below it, both aligned left edges. Column 4: SETS centred vertically between PROC and BASE. Column 5: TERM1/TERM2/TERM3 stacked, then SUM, SCORE and DELTA continuing to the right (SUM and SCORE may share a row at far right). CTRL sits along the bottom of columns 3-5 as a horizontal strip with VALID at its right end, below BASE and the scoring stack, with its dashed edge going up to SCORE. The EVAL container wraps columns 1-2, BASE, SETS-side scoring and CTRL but not PROC; if wrapping is awkward, render EVAL as a small corner tag 'Evaluator-owned' on each of DATA, BASE, scoring stack and CTRL (identical small tag) and omit the container. NOREAL sits just outside the bottom-right corner of SCOPE.

IMPORTANCE RANKING: 1) PROC (the studied object), 2) the scoring stack with weights and SCORE, 3) BASE, 4) SETS and DATA/CAL/TEST, 5) CTRL and VALID, 6) SCOPE boundary and NOREAL (quiet but unmistakable), 7) DELTA.
